name: Madison Metropolitan School District

seoTitle: Madison Metropolitan School District Calendar: MMSD Dates
seoDescription: Reviewed MMSD dates, staggered opening, school-level conferences, grading periods, religious observances, bell schedules, and graduations.
districtFact: Madison Metropolitan School District starts the year in two stages: 4K, kindergarten, grades 6 and 9, and Early Childhood attend first, then every student follows the regular schedule the next day. Bell schedules vary by school and should be checked against the district’s current start and dismissal table.

about.title: A Transition-Grade Opening
about.content: MMSD gives 4K, kindergarten, grades 6 and 9, and Early Childhood the first student day. All grades attend their regular schedule the next day. The pattern creates a quieter transition for students entering elementary, middle, and high school rather than one universal first-day experience.

about.title: Bell Schedules Vary by School
about.content: Start and dismissal times vary across MMSD schools and may change between school years. Families should use the district’s current school-by-school start and dismissal table rather than treating a past schedule rule as permanent.

about.title: Conferences Are Scheduled by School Level
about.content: Elementary, middle, and high school conferences do not share one closure date. Each level has its own conference schedule and no-school dates, while high schools also receive separate professional-learning dates. A sibling in another level may still attend school.

about.title: Religious Observances Guide Scheduling, Not Automatic Closure
about.content: Under Board Policy 4039, schools avoid significant exams, athletic contests, assemblies, field trips, and similar special events on observances likely to affect attendance. The religious calendar is therefore a planning layer; an observance should not be converted into a districtwide no-school day unless the school-year calendar says so.

about.title: Quarter Dates Sit Inside Two Semesters
about.content: MMSD publishes four quarter boundaries and two semester boundaries. The second quarter closes with semester one, followed by a staff grading day; the fourth quarter closes with semester two on the full final student day.

calendarNotes: MMSD's main calendar applies districtwide, but several dates affect only elementary, middle, or high school students. The first student day is for 4K, kindergarten, grades 6 and 9, and Early Childhood; all students follow the regular schedule the next day. School start and dismissal times are maintained separately and can change by school year. Conference evenings and no-school days are separated by school level. Quarter and semester boundaries create staff grading or staff-only days. Religious observances guide assessment and event scheduling but are not automatic closures. The district says snow days are built into the calendar and may convert a scheduled Staff Only Day to a school day if all allotted snow days are used. Graduation dates differ among Shabazz, Innovative, Capital, East, La Follette, Memorial, and West high schools.

planningTips.title: Planning with the MMSD Calendar
content: Use the first September date only for 4K, kindergarten, grades 6 and 9, and Early Childhood; all other grades begin their regular schedule the following day.
Check the current school-by-school start and dismissal table before planning pickup; bell-time rules can change between school years.
Check every conference date against the student's level because elementary, middle, and high schools close on different days.
Do not treat the religious holiday calendar as a closure list; it identifies dates when schools should avoid major exams and special events.
Keep Staff Only Days flexible in weather planning because MMSD may use one as a student day after all built-in snow days are exhausted.
For siblings at different campuses, use the school-by-school start and dismissal table rather than assuming one district bell schedule.
Confirm graduation details with the high school because ceremony dates are grouped by campus and some future dates are tentative.

livingHere.intro: MMSD is a city-centered district whose school choices, transition grades, and calendar layers reflect Madison's university, government, and multilingual community.

highlights.label: 52 schools
highlights.detail: The district profile describes a network of 52 schools serving Madison-area students.

highlights.label: About 25,000 students
highlights.detail: MMSD identifies itself as Wisconsin's second-largest school district.

highlights.label: 4K in public and private settings
highlights.detail: The district offers tuition-free four-year-old kindergarten through a community-based early-learning network.

highlights.label: Early college pathways
highlights.detail: Official options include biotechnology, education, networking and cybersecurity, STEM, and Running Start academies.

highlights.label: Multiple daily bell schedules
highlights.detail: Elementary start times include 7:35 and 8:25 a.m. groups, with distinct Monday dismissal times.

highlights.label: Six named graduation groups
highlights.detail: The annual calendar separately schedules Shabazz, Innovative, Capital, East, La Follette, Memorial, and West ceremonies.

districtFaqs.q: Do all MMSD students start school on the same day?
districtFaqs.a: No. 4K, kindergarten, grades 6 and 9, and Early Childhood attend the first day. All students follow their regular schedule the next day.

districtFaqs.q: Who has early release on Mondays in Madison schools?
districtFaqs.a: Monday early-release eligibility can change by school year. Check MMSD’s current school-by-school start and dismissal table rather than relying on an earlier year’s rule.

districtFaqs.q: Are MMSD family-teacher conference days districtwide closures?
districtFaqs.a: No. Elementary, middle, and high schools have different conference schedules and no-school dates.

districtFaqs.q: Does MMSD close for every religious holiday on its calendar?
districtFaqs.a: No. A religious observance listed by MMSD does not by itself mean school is closed. Check the school-year calendar for no-school dates.

districtFaqs.q: Can an MMSD Staff Only Day become a school day?
districtFaqs.a: Potentially. MMSD says snow days are built into the calendar; if all are used, the district will likely hold school on a scheduled Staff Only Day.

districtFaqs.q: Does MMSD use quarters or semesters?
districtFaqs.a: Both. The calendar publishes four quarters nested inside two semesters. Quarter two ends with semester one, and quarter four ends with semester two.

customSections.label: Four Calendar Layers Families Need
customSections.content: No single MMSD page answers every scheduling question. Combining the right layers prevents a level-specific closure or Monday dismissal from being misread.

customSections.label: Staff Only Days Are the Weather Reserve
customSections.content: MMSD says snow days are already built into the adopted calendar. If every allotted snow day is used, the district will likely convert a scheduled Staff Only Day into a school day. Families should wait for an official announcement rather than assuming a specific reserve date has been activated.
